title: PromptTemplatesResponse
description: The prompt templates this tenant offers for /v1/query generation (ADR-0008). Templates are deployment configuration loaded and validated at startup, not user content: a caller SELECTS one and fills its declared slots, and can never supply prompt text of its own. A server with no templates configured answers with an empty list, which is how a client learns the capability is absent without a version check.

id.description: The value a caller passes as `template` on /v1/query. Bounded by the contract because it is caller-supplied and reaches logs: lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens and underscores.

version.description: Bumped on ANY content change. With `id` and `hash` it names the condition a result was produced under, which is what lets an ablation arm hold generation fixed.

hash.description: Content hash of the template SOURCE — the bytes that reach the model plus the rules that decide what is accepted — computed at load. Not of a rendered body: rendering depends on a request's template_vars, so a rendered hash could not be computed at load and would differ per call. Because templates are per-tenant and copied by hand, two tenants can hold the same (id, version) with bodies that have drifted apart; comparing hashes is how that is detected rather than silently mis-attributed. Display-only strings (`label`) are excluded, so renaming a picker entry does not read as drift.

output.description: The shape the template asks the model for. `table` declares `columns`; `text` is prose. Advisory to the client for rendering — the response's `answer` is the model's raw text either way, since a model may not comply and the server does not parse it (ADR-0008 consequences).

columns.description: Column names when `output` is `table`; absent otherwise.

slots.description: The named values this template accepts in `template_vars`. A slot not declared here is a 422 rather than being ignored, because a typo'd name that renders an empty clause produces a subtly wrong prompt and no error.

max_len.description: Maximum accepted length of the value. Declared per slot and mandatory: an organism name is not an essay, and an undeclared cap is a template authoring error that fails at load rather than at request time.

max_output_tokens.description: Ceiling on GENERATED tokens for this template; absent means the server's llm_max_output_tokens applies. A table template needs materially more room than a prose one — it asks for as many rows as the literature supports, and a cap comfortable for a paragraph truncates the table mid-row.

allOf.description: `columns` is required when output is `table` and forbidden when it is `text`. Stated as a constraint rather than only in prose, so a server that emits columns on a prose template fails validation instead of quietly shipping a field a client will try to render a table from.
